places.name: March of Pacified Borders
places.summary: The empire's frontier march, 12,000 li of hill country ruled by the Gongsun family of generals: some forty million farmers who plow with spears at hand, and a line of beacon peaks whose spirit-fire carries a raid warning across the march in a night.
places.lore: The Gongsuns have held the march for nine generations and buried most of their sons on the wall. Every family owes one child to the garrison at sixteen, which keeps a million and a half under arms across the march, the [[Wall of Piled Bones]] and the coast. Rooted children are another matter: since the raids tripled, the Gongsuns hold a frontier charter, so the Registry's frontier tester comes at twelve, the age the march can put a child on the wall, and the garrison keeps every rooted child for its cadet school instead of sending them to the capital. Its best leave all the same, for the City of the Guarded Mouth or the Beast-Butcher Gate, so the march itself has no one past Foundation. Children here learn to read beast tracks before letters and to tell a raid horn from a hunt horn. A beast core turned in at a fort earns a bounty in rice or stones.

features.name: a village watchtower
a beast-pit
fields plowed with spears at hand

places.name: The Wall of Piled Bones
places.summary: A wall of rammed earth and beast-king bone 9,000 li long along the coastal hills, as tall as cliffs and built over a thousand years of raids. On Ghost Month nights the bones howl.
places.lore: Each garrison builds in the bones of the beasts it kills, and the oldest stretches are faced with the skulls of beast kings, each the size of a hill, their eye sockets now the wall's gates. Binding arrays run along the top as a thread of light and hold the beast spirits down, all but the seventh month, when they haunt it and ghost-hunters and bone-collectors come. Old bones from the wall are a refining material for beast-taming whistles and Slaughter Dao artifacts, and stealing them is a hanging offense. The [[March of Pacified Borders]] garrisons the southern stretch, and its cadets learn the wall by patrolling it.

features.name: the patrol walk along the top
the old stretches faced with beast-king skulls, their eye sockets gates
bone heaps waiting to be built in

places.name: Realm of Mingled Blood
places.summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a karst cave every seven years. It admits only those below Foundation who carry beast blood, or a tamer bonded to a beast.
places.lore: Inside is a green world where beasts and humans once lived as one people, with ruined villages, bloodline altars and herbs that awaken dormant bloodlines. Half-bloods go in to learn what they are; tamers go in to strengthen their bonds; pure humans who try the gate are thrown back with broken bones. The Night Bridge Society guards the cave and charges entry. It last opened five years ago.

features.name: the gate cave in the karst
a ruined village of the one people
a bloodline altar
herb meadows under a green sky

places.name: Soul-Lost Stone Forest
places.summary: A maze of stone pillars 12,000 li across, each pillar a peak in its own right, where a great python from the Vast Wilds Continent has made its den. Its illusions turn the forest into a trap no map survives.
places.lore: The Golden Python's grandson, a Nascent Soul serpent several li long, crossed the strait six years ago and took the stone forest as its hunting ground. Its illusions make travelers walk in circles until they starve. A shed skin of its is worth a fortune, and its den is said to hold the treasures of everyone it has eaten. Three imperial expeditions have gone in.

features.name: stone pillars that shift in the illusion
narrow lanes between the pillars
the python's den

places.name: Kingdom of Spirit Herders
places.summary: A kingdom of beast tamers on 9,000 li of grassland, who raise war mounts for the empire by the hundred thousand from eggs smuggled out of the Vast Wilds Continent. The Beast Court has put a price on every one of them.
places.lore: The Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches raise thunder-horned deer, scale-horses and war hounds from eggs and cubs bought from smugglers, in herds that take days to ride past. The empire buys every mount at a good price, and the herder families are rich, armed and hunted. Beast Court agents, half-bloods in its pay and now and then an old beast, cross the strait to kill tamers and free their beasts. Children are bonded to a hatchling at seven and grow up with it.

features.name: ranch corrals of thunder-horned deer and scale-horses
open grass to the horizon
the hatchling barns

places.name: Kingdom of Stone Eyes
places.summary: Nine thousand li of sinkhole karst ruled by a council of cave clans. The great sinkholes hold whole towns down their walls; half-blood families hide here, and nobody asks what is in the lower caves.
places.lore: Stone Eyes is named for the round sinkholes that pock its karst. The great ones are tens of li across, each a town terraced down its walls with the farms at the bottom; the small ones hold a village each. Its people farm in the sinkholes, keep bats for guano and guide smugglers through caves that run for thousands of li and that no map shows. The empire counts it as part of the march; the cave clans pay no tax and give no soldiers. Children grow up knowing which neighbors have scales under their sleeves and never saying so.

features.name: a sinkhole rim with terraces down the walls
caves no map shows
bat roosts heaped with guano

places.name: City of the Guarded Mouth
places.summary: The empire's frontier headquarters, a fortress city of eight million on the coast where the island chain begins. Its walls rise out of the surf as tall as sea cliffs, faced with the skulls of the beast kings that tried them.
places.lore: The City of the Guarded Mouth holds the narrow coast where the chain begins, a ring of walls 150 li across with a garrison of three hundred thousand soldiers and five thousand cultivators, under a commander who has reached Nascent Soul. A ward array caps the harbour mouth, and its bounty office pays for cores by grade. Its markets sell beast parts, smuggled Vast Wilds herbs and frontier saber steel. Every sect with a frontier interest keeps a hall here. At low tide, the reef road appears below the walls.

features.name: the sea-cliff walls, faced with beast-king skulls
the bounty office, paying for cores by grade
the beast-part market
the reef road below the walls at low tide

places.name: Beast-Butcher Gate
places.summary: A frontier sect of three thousand saber cultivators who raid across the strait for beast cores, on three peaks its founder sheared flat with one cut. Brutal, rich and the beasts' favorite target.
places.lore: The Beast-Butcher Gate teaches Saber and Slaughter Daos and recruits frontier orphans who have already lost someone to beasts. Disciples earn rank by cores taken. The sect sells cores to the Apricot Grove Valley, hides to the Zhu clan's rivals and meat to anyone, and leads the empire's punitive raids across the island chain. It despises beast tamers as collaborators and half-bloods as vermin.

features.name: the drill yard, where rank is counted in cores
the core vault
racks of frontier sabers

places.name: Night Bridge Society
places.summary: Half-blood smugglers who run the island chain in relays, one crew to a stretch, passing people, Gu eggs, beast cubs and herbs from island to island at low tide between the Morning Star Continent and Shared Roost City.
places.lore: The Society knows the tides, the reefs and which islands have something living on them this month. Most of its runners are Qi Condensation or Foundation half-bloods who know one stretch by heart, and each crew waits on its own tide, so a cargo takes about half a year to pass end to end; only the Core Formation leaders fly the whole chain, in about a month. It runs half-bloods out of human villages, beast eggs to the Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches, Gu to the marsh and Vast Wilds herbs to anyone. Its leaders are half-bloods with beast senses and long grudges. It pays tribute to nobody and has informers in every fort. Passage costs five low-grade stones, or a favor.

features.name: a tide pool island on the chain
the low-tide reef between islands
a smugglers' sea cave

places.name: Thousand Paddocks
places.summary: The Spirit Herders' royal city, three million people inside a ring of array-fenced paddocks sixty li across, where the king holds court on horseback and the empire's remount officers keep a standing hall.
places.lore: Thousand Paddocks grew out of the first ranch, and the royal family still counts its wealth in heads. The paddocks are fenced with formation posts that keep a war mount in and a raiding beast out, and the court moves among them by season. Every great herder family keeps a hall here and sends its best riders to the king's games each autumn, where the empire's officers buy by the thousand. The Hundred Reins Sect's tamers bond the royal stud, and the Beast Court has twice sent killers into the palace paddocks.

features.name: the array-fenced paddocks
the king's riding court
the remount officers' hall

places.name: River-Bend City
places.summary: The March's biggest market, three million people in a bend of the river below Grain Ford, where the garrison buys, the counties sell and the Gongsuns' tax barges load.
places.lore: River-Bend City is where the March's grain, iron and conscripts meet the money that pays for them. Its markets run fifty li along the bend, and its wharves load the barges that carry the levy downriver to the capital. The Gongsuns rule it through an intendant, the Qian clan's agents buy the March's cores here before they reach the City, and every county sends its sixteen-year-olds through its muster yards.

features.name: the muster yards
the tax wharves on the bend
the grain market

places.name: Ebb Harbor
places.summary: A strait port of a million on the Tidewrack Shore, where the island chain's first reef runs out at low tide. Honest cargo goes out on the tide; the rest goes out on the Night Bridge.
places.lore: Ebb Harbor's breakwaters are old reef lifted and bound by a dead sect's array, and its harbor drains to mud twice a day, leaving the ships sitting on it. It ships salt, hides and the March's grain to the forts on the chain, and takes in what comes back. The harbormaster answers to the City of the Guarded Mouth, and the City's inspectors are paid to count only what they see.

features.name: the bound-reef breakwaters
the harbor floor at low tide
the east quay warehouses

places.name: Heaven's Eye
places.summary: The greatest sinkhole in Stone Eyes, sixty li across and five million people terraced down its walls, where the council of cave clans meets in a hall cut into the cliff halfway down.
places.lore: Heaven's Eye is the sinkhole the kingdom is named for: seen from a flying sword it looks up at the sky like an eye. Its terraces drop two li to fields at the bottom that never see noon, and its council hall is cut into the north wall halfway down, reached only by the clans' own stairs. Each cave clan holds a stretch of the wall and a vote, and the council's one law is that nobody asks what anybody keeps below the bottom terrace.

features.name: the terraces down the sinkhole wall
the council hall in the cliff
the fields at the bottom that never see noon

places.name: The Nameless Market
places.summary: A free market of two hundred thousand in a karst valley of the Southern Karst that no sect, clan or crown rules: rogue cultivators sell what they found, took or stole, and nobody asks whose it was.
places.lore: The Nameless Market has no walls, no tax and no name, because naming a thing invites someone to claim it. Two thousand rogue cultivators pass through it in a season, trading cores, herbs, maps of ruins and the belongings of people who did not come back. Its one rule is that blood spilled inside the valley is paid for, and an old Core Formation rogue called Uncle Ash collects the payment. The sects call it a den of thieves and buy there all the same.

features.name: stalls on the valley floor under the pillars
Uncle Ash's tea shed
caves rented by the night

places.name: Pavilion of Bound Bones
places.summary: An array sect of two and a half thousand that the empire pays to keep the Wall of Piled Bones' binding arrays lit, so the beast spirits in its bones stay down all but one month a year.
places.lore: The Pavilion of Bound Bones was founded to bind the Wall's dead, and the empire's stipend has kept it doing nothing else for six hundred years. Its disciples walk the Wall's 9,000 li in relays, renewing the array along the top, and its hall stands in the eye socket of the greatest skull in the Wall. In Ghost Month the arrays are let down on purpose, because holding them all year cracks the bones, and the Pavilion spends the month with the Temple of the Quiet Bell quieting what comes up. It wants the Black Jade Vein's jade for its array plates, and so does the Beast-Butcher Gate.

features.name: the hall in the great skull's eye socket
the array plates along the Wall's top
the bone-reading room

places.name: Hundred Reins Sect
places.summary: A beast-taming sect of three thousand that the Spirit Herders back, teaching the bond between rider and beast as a Dao. It is in a blood feud with the Beast-Butcher Gate, who call it the collaborators' sect.
places.lore: The Hundred Reins Sect bonds its disciples to beasts the way the Herders bond their children, but as cultivation: a disciple and a beast cultivate as one, and the strongest pairs fight as a single cultivator a realm above either. It trains the royal stud at Thousand Paddocks and the Herders pay its keep. The Beast-Butcher Gate kills tamed beasts on sight as Beast Court spies, the Reins kill butchers who do it, and the feud has run a hundred and twenty years. Its elders want a thunder-ape cub from Ape-Cry Peaks, and three teams have died trying.

features.name: the bonding stables
the open grass where pairs spar
the hatchery kept warm by array

places.name: Temple of the Quiet Bell
places.summary: A Buddhist temple of a few hundred monks in the Bonefields that buries the raids' dead, mortal and beast alike, and quiets the Wall each Ghost Month with a bell that is only ever struck once a year.
places.lore: The Quiet Bell's monks bury whatever the raids leave, beasts included, which the Beast-Butcher Gate takes as an insult and the Herders as a kindness. Their bell hangs in a tower cut from a single bone and is struck once at the start of Ghost Month; its note carries the length of the Wall, and the spirits that rise hear it. They keep the battlefield at the Broken Tide quiet as well, and ask no fee from anyone.

features.name: the bell tower of one bone
the burial fields
the meditation caves

places.name: Lamp-Keeper Sect
places.summary: A ghost-way sect of five hundred that keeps the lamps of the Ghost-Lamp Fens lit, so the drowned stay in the water instead of walking to the City of the Guarded Mouth.
places.lore: The Ghost-Lamp Fens are named for the sect's lamps: ten thousand of them on poles across the water, burning yin fire that the drowned follow in circles instead of walking out. The City of the Guarded Mouth pays the sect to keep them lit, and has since the night a lamp line failed and the dead came to its walls. The Lamp-Keepers cultivate on the fens' yin qi, speak to the drowned, and sell what the drowned tell them.

features.name: lamp poles across the black water
the stilt hall in the fens
the drowned, circling under the lamps

places.name: Red Marrow Cave
places.summary: A rumor of a demonic sect in the Grey Karst Reaches that keeps beasts in pens underground and drains their blood for pills that let a cultivator climb fast and die young.
places.lore: Hunters in the Grey Karst Reaches tell of caves that smell of iron and of beasts heard bellowing under the ground with no beast in sight. Blood pills that turn up at the Nameless Market are said to come from there. Nobody who has gone looking has said where it is.

features.name: beast pens a li underground
the blood pools
a cave mouth that smells of iron

places.name: The Hu Clan
places.summary: A cave clan of Stone Eyes, forty thousand strong with three hundred cultivators, that holds a stretch of Heaven's Eye's wall and a council vote. Its people are handsome and quick, and none of them stands long in front of a mirror array.
places.lore: The Hu clan has guided travelers through the lower caves for longer than Stone Eyes has had a council, and its children are the best cave guides in the kingdom. It marries inside the clan, buries its own dead in caves nobody else enters, and sends a child to the Registry's testing stone only when the tester is someone it knows.

features.name: the clan's stretch of the sinkhole wall
burial caves nobody else enters

places.name: The Qian Clan
places.summary: A cultivating merchant clan of the City of the Guarded Mouth that sits between the bounty office, the Beast-Butcher Gate and Apricot Grove Valley's buyers, and takes a cut of every beast core that leaves the Border Wilds.
places.lore: The Qians came to the frontier four generations ago with one shop and a contract for Gate cores, and now hold the City's core exchange. Their agents buy at River-Bend and the forts before cores reach the bounty office, grade them, and sell the best to Apricot Grove Valley's frontier hall. They are polite to everyone and owe nobody, and a cultivator short of stones can always sell them a future.

features.name: the core exchange, graded by lamp
the clan vault under the exchange

places.name: Apricot Grove's Frontier Hall
places.summary: Apricot Grove Valley's branch hall in the City of the Guarded Mouth, which buys the frontier's beast cores for the Valley's furnaces and sells healing pills to anyone, at prices the frontier complains about and pays.
places.lore: The Frontier Hall is a pill shop, a clinic and a buying office under one green roof. Its physicians treat garrison soldiers free once a year by the Valley's old promise, and its buyers take the cores the Qian clan grades. Its master is a Core Formation physician posted from the Valley, who would rather be home.

features.name: the clinic hall
the pill counter

places.name: Ape-Cry Peaks
places.summary: A tract of needle peaks seven thousand li across ruled by a troop of thunder-apes, whose king has formed his core. Their cries carry for a hundred li before a storm, and lightning follows them.
places.lore: The thunder-apes came over the strait three hundred years ago and took the Needle Peaks from whatever held them. The troop is some three thousand strong, ruled by a Core Formation king who calls storms down on anyone who climbs above the cloud line. Their cubs are worth a fortune to tamers and their thunder-bone to refiners, and the Black Jade Vein runs under their southern peaks.

features.name: needle peaks above the cloud line
storm-blackened ledges where the troop sits
the king's peak, its top split by lightning

places.name: Jiao Gorge
places.summary: A river gorge five thousand li long through the Mistbamboo Hollows where a flood-jiao has made its lair. Each spring it rises with the snowmelt and floods the sinkholes of Stone Eyes downriver.
places.lore: The flood-jiao is a Foundation beast a li long, halfway to a dragon by its own reckoning and nowhere near by anyone else's. It lies in the gorge's deep pools, and each spring it rides the snowmelt down and the river comes over the sinkhole rims with it. Stone Eyes has sent cultivators to kill it four times and buried them all. Its shed scales are prized by the City's armorers.

features.name: the deep pools under the gorge walls
the gorge walls hung with mist-bamboo
the jiao's sloughed scales on the gravel

places.name: Field of the Broken Tide
places.summary: Salt flats three hundred li across on the southern coast where the empire first held the shore against a beast tide a thousand years ago. The tide's dead and the empire's still stand where they fell.
places.lore: A thousand years ago a beast tide came over the chain and the empire met it on the flats with forty thousand cultivators and a million soldiers. The line held and the flats have been white with salt and bone ever since. On still nights the armies form up again, and the Temple of the Quiet Bell keeps them from marching. Scavengers dig old artifacts out of the salt; most of them come back.

features.name: salt flats white with bone
the ghost armies forming up on still nights
artifacts in the salt

places.name: Ruins of the Starfall Sect
places.summary: The ruins of a sect that ruled the Border Wilds eight hundred years ago until a beast tide broke its mountain, sunk in the Blackpine Forest. Its halls are rubble; what it kept underneath is not.
places.lore: The Starfall Sect drew its arts from a fallen star and held the frontier for three thousand years. Eight hundred years ago a beast tide led by a king of the Vast Wilds broke its mountain in a night, and the forest has grown over the pieces. Scavengers still find star-iron in the rubble. Every few decades the ground at the heart of the ruins glows, and those who go in when it does come out changed, or not at all.

features.name: broken halls under blackpines
star-iron in the rubble
the glowing ground at the heart

places.name: Black Jade Vein
places.summary: A spirit-jade vein under the southern Ape-Cry Peaks, the richest in the Border Wilds, mined in galleries the Pavilion of Bound Bones and the Beast-Butcher Gate each claim, while the thunder-apes bring the mountain down on both.
places.lore: Black jade holds an array's charge better than any stone on the frontier and takes a saber's edge like steel, so two sects want all of it. The Pavilion's miners hold the upper galleries and the Gate's the lower, and the shafts between are where they fight. Above both, the thunder-apes drop rock on anyone they hear digging.

features.name: galleries cut through black jade
the contested middle shafts
spoil heaps at the gallery mouths

places.name: Starfall Remnant
places.summary: The Starfall Sect's last hall, folded into a pocket of space under its ruins when the mountain broke. It opens for ten days every thirty years, when the ground at the ruins' heart glows.
places.lore: When the beast tide broke the mountain, the Starfall Sect's last elders folded their library and their star into a pocket of space and sealed themselves in with it. Every thirty years the seal thins, and cultivators below Core Formation can slip through. Inside are the sect's halls as they were, the arts it drew from its star, and the guardians it left.

features.name: the halls as they were the night the mountain fell
the star in its vault
the guardians the elders left
